title: Why? #5: why a spoon shows you upside down (concave mirror, live rays) → NDA 2026 (I) GAT Q64 (48 s, calm music)

captions.instagram:
Why? #5 · Why does a spoon show you upside down? 🥄

The inside of a spoon is a concave mirror. Stand far away and the reflected rays cross before they reach your eye, so your image is upside down. Walk closer: the image moves from F towards C and grows. At F there's no image at all. Come closer than F and the rays never cross: you're upright and bigger. That's the flip.

NDA 2026 (I) asked it (GAT Physics Q64): an object far beyond C of a concave mirror accelerates towards it. Which is correct?
Far away, the image sits near F; as the object reaches C, the image moves from F to C, faster and faster → (a) the image accelerates towards C.
